text.p: Australia's largest brewer, Foster's Brewing Group Ltd, on Wednesday painted a robust picture for the future of its domestic wine and beer units while pledging improvement from offshore divisions.

Foster's net profit for the year to June 30 rose two percent to A$293.3 million. "The directors believe that the profit provides a strong platform for the company to build on in future years," Foster's said in its annual report.
But the company warned that its Australian earnings would face higher taxes in 1996/97 as it would exhaust the benefits from previous years' tax losses during the period.
Foster's said its major unit, Carlton & United Breweries, would underpin group profit growth by continuing to increase operating efficiencies and further develop its leisure and hospitality strategy.
Its winemaker Mildara Blass was forecast to have good future growth in profits, volume and return on investments.

"The 1996 vintage produced record tonnages for Mildara Blass ... and this places the company in a good position to satisfy projected demand in the future, including that for red wines," Foster's said.
Foster's said its 40-percent owned Canadian brewer Molson Breweries was expected to post higher profits on the back of lower overheads associated with its restructure.
Molson posted a 55 percent slump in net profit for the year to April 1 after writing off restructuring costs, contributing A$61 million to Foster's 1996/96 bottom line.

Foster's said it would maintain investment in its Chinese brewing joint venture in the areas of sales, marketing and distribution. Foster's said its was encouraged that peak demand in Shanghai and Tianjin sometimes outstripped supply.
